subject: Take-home release + reviewer roster / submission flow
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Zhao <ethan.zhao@gmail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood take-home: Systems inference exercise — instructions & deadline

Hi Ethan,

Thanks again for taking the time to interview with us. Attached is the take-home assignment for the Senior Inference Engineer role (assignment.pdf). It should take ~4–6 hours; we ask for a runnable submission and a short write-up describing design tradeoffs and any performance assumptions.

Key details:
- Deadline: Tue, 9 Jun 2027 23:59 PT (please submit before then)
- Deliverable: one ZIP with code + README OR a private Drive link with instructions (we prefer runnable examples)
- File name convention: lastname_firstname_submission.zip
- Where to submit: reply-all with the Drive link or attach the ZIP to your reply

Reviewer plan: Laura and Marcus will be the primary reviewers; Marissa will provide a tie-break / infra review if needed. We’ve attached the review rubric (review_rubric.md) to help you understand what we’re looking for.

One clarification up front: standard library + PyTorch/TensorFlow is fine. Avoid calling paid external APIs in the submission (we need reproducibility). If you want to use a specific quantization library not listed, flag it in the README.

Please reply to confirm you received the assignment and whether the deadline works. If you need an extension, note it in your reply — we can sometimes grant a 48-hour extension for extenuating circumstances.

Best of luck,
Chloe Martin
Hiring Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- assignment.pdf (PDF)
- review_rubric.md (text)

From: Ethan Zhao <ethan.zhao@gmail.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood take-home: Systems inference exercise — instructions & deadline

Chloe — thanks, I got the assignment and rubric. Deadline works for me.

Quick question: is it OK to include compiled artifacts (e.g., a small Wheel or a prebuilt quantized model) as long as I document how they were produced? I want reviewers to be able to run inference locally without long build steps.

Thanks,
Ethan

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Reviewer slots for Ethan Zhao take-home (assignments + plan)

Team — FYI: I sent Ethan the take-home yesterday and he confirmed. He’ll submit by EOD Tue 9 Jun PT. Please volunteer for reviewer slots below:

Proposed reviewer workflow:
- Primary reviewer A: first pass for correctness and approach (30–45m)
- Primary reviewer B: run tests and evaluate reproducibility (30–45m)
- Tie-break / infra pass: perf assumptions, infra implications (15–30m)

Tentative availability (I’ll book calendar blocks once people confirm):
- Wed 10 Jun 10:00–11:30 PT — run-through + notes (pair review if possible)
- Thu 11 Jun 14:00–15:30 PT — finalize scoring and calibration

Please reply with: 1) which primary role you’ll take (A/B), 2) whether you can attend the Wed block, and 3) any conflicts. I’ve uploaded the rubric and a placeholder folder with the assignment to: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/TA-ethan-zhao-2027

Thanks — trying to keep this light-touch and consistent with other TA workflows.

-Chloe

Subject: Re: Redwood take-home: Systems inference exercise — submission

Chloe / team — I uploaded my submission here: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/TA-ethan-zhao-2027/submission_v1

Files in the folder:
- ethan_zhao_submission.zip (contains code + README + small prebuilt wheel for quick run)
- run_instructions.md
- small_quantized_model.pt

Notes:
- The wheel is included solely for convenience; README includes steps to rebuild from source if you prefer.
- I tested the example on a single V100 briefly — inference latency and memory notes are in the README.

Please let me know if you can’t access the folder or want me to attach the zip directly to the email.

Thanks — looking forward to feedback,
Ethan
